question: What constitutes the manufacturing sector in Uganda and how are manufacturers regulated and registered?
answer: Manufacturing involves transforming raw materials, chemical components, or intermediate parts into finished tangible goods through mechanical, thermal, or chemical processing. In Uganda, manufactured tangible products span steel & metals, plastics, food & beverages, cosmetics, textiles & garments, pharmaceuticals, building materials, stationery, and vehicle assembly. Regulatory framework requires: 1) Business incorporation with URSB; 2) Uganda National Bureau of Standards (UNBS) Distinctive Mark / Quality Certification; 3) NEMA environmental clearance; 4) Uganda Investment Authority (UIA) investment license for industrial park operations; 5) URA Tax Identification Number (TIN) with registration for Corporation Tax (30%), PAYE, VAT (18%), Local Excise Duty, and Digital Tax Stamps (DTS).

question: What are the eligibility criteria and benefits of the 10-year income tax holiday for manufacturers in Uganda?
answer: Under Section 21(1)(y) and 21(1)(z) of the Income Tax Act and the Manufacturing Sector Guide: 1) Qualifying Activities: Manufacturing or assembling building materials, pharmaceuticals, medical appliances, automobiles, household appliances, furniture, pulp/paper, agricultural/industrial chemicals, textiles, glassware, leather, tyres, sanitary pads, or processing agricultural products in an Industrial Park or Free Zone; 2) Capital Investment Thresholds: Minimum USD 10 million for foreign investors, USD 300,000 for EAC citizens, or USD 150,000 for citizen investments located upcountry outside a 50 km radius from Kampala; 3) Local Content & Labor: Must use at least 50% locally sourced raw materials (subject to availability) and employ at least 100 Ugandan citizens (or 70% of staff being citizens); 4) Exporters: Manufacturers outside industrial parks who export at least 80% of finished consumer or capital goods also receive a 10-year income tax holiday.

question: How does the East African Community Duty Remission Scheme apply to manufacturing raw materials and industrial inputs?
answer: Under Section 130 and 140 of the EACCMA and EAC Duty Remission Regulations: 1) Manufacturers in Uganda can import designated industrial raw materials, active ingredients, and packaging supplies at preferential 0% or 10% duty rates (down from 25% or 35%) under gazetted Duty Remission quotas approved by the EAC Council of Ministers; 2) Key Covered Sectors: Cosmetics manufacturing (clear primers, chemical bases, essential oils); Food and beverage processing (glucose syrup, food additives, specialized packaging); Steel sector (steel billets, wire rod, scrap); Textile and garment manufacturing (raw yarn, weaving fabrics); CKD unassembled vehicle kits; and paints/varnishes; 3) EACCMA Fifth Schedule Part B Item 31: Replacement spare parts for industrial machinery (Chapters 84 & 85) are exempt from all import duties and taxes under Additional Procedure Code APC 492 with MTIC/UMA recommendation.

question: What VAT exemptions, deemed VAT rules, and input credits apply to manufacturing plant, machinery, and raw materials?
answer: Under the VAT Act and Manufacturing Guide: 1) Plant & Machinery: Importation or local supply of industrial plant and machinery for use in manufacturing attracts 0% import duty and is VAT-exempt / deemed paid; 2) Raw Material Supplies in Industrial Parks: Supply of locally produced raw materials to a manufacturer in an Industrial Park or Free Zone is exempt from VAT; 3) Input Tax Credit: VAT-registered manufacturers are entitled to full input VAT deduction on taxable supplies, raw materials, commercial electricity, and utilities used in making taxable supplies; 4) Deemed VAT for Aid Projects: Tax payable on supplies to contractors executing aid-funded industrial projects is deemed paid under Section 24(5) VAT Act; 5) Nil Excise Duty: Construction materials supplied to an industrial park or free zone developer/operator bear Nil excise duty.

question: Which manufactured goods require Digital Tax Stamps (DTS) in Uganda and what are the compliance rules for factory lines?
answer: Under the Tax Procedures Code (Tax Stamps) Regulations, manufacturers of gazetted excisable commodities must affix and activate physical Digital Tax Stamps (or digital ink-jet codes) on every unit at production packaging lines: 1) Gazetted Products: Beer, spirits/liquor, wine, carbonated soft drinks, bottled mineral water, tobacco products, cement, and sugar; 2) Direct Line Integration: Manufacturers must install high-speed production line stamping applicators and camera vision verification scanners connected in real-time to the URA DTS central monitoring system; 3) Production Accounting: Production volumes recorded by DTS directly reconcile with monthly Local Excise Duty and VAT returns; 4) Sanctions: Selling or distributing unstamped gazetted goods attracts mandatory seizure, 100% penal tax of the tax value, and factory closure.

question: What statutory tax rules specifically apply to cosmetics processing, steel mills, food & beverages, and textile processing?
answer: 1) Cosmetics Processing: Inputs for toiletries and beauty products enjoy duty remission under gazetted quotas; hazardous cosmetics containing mercury or hydroquinone are strictly prohibited from manufacture or importation under Section 200 EACCMA; 2) Steel Mills: Steel billets, wire rods, and scrap metal imported for re-rolling and fabrication benefit from EAC industrial tariffs; local steel supply attracts standard 18% VAT and 6% WHT on non-exempt contracts; 3) Food & Beverages: Processed milk, unprocessed cereals, and raw foodstuffs are VAT-exempt; packaged juices, confectioneries, and alcoholic beverages attract Local Excise Duty and mandatory DTS; 4) Textile & Apparel: Weaving fabrics and sewing thread imported for export garment manufacturing (under AGOA or regional EAC market) benefit from duty remission; locally grown and ginned lint cotton is VAT-exempt.
